In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah Lam Yakun (Surah 98)

It is Meccan according to some scholars, and Medinan according to others, and Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to desist﴾. Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited: "مَا كَانَ الَّذين كفرُوا" ("Those who disbelieved were not..."), and this is shadhdh (an irregular, non-canonical reading), while the well-known reading is the first one.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿from the People of the Book and the polytheists, [who were] separate [from their disbelief]﴾. That is, "munthahin" (desisting, refraining). Its meaning is that the disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not desisting from their disbelief until the clear proof (al-bayyinah) came to them, that is, until the Messenger came to them, with the future tense used in the sense of the past. It has also been said: the clear proof is the Qur'an, and this is a well-known and relied-upon opinion. The second opinion is that the People of the Book and the polytheists who had heard from them [about the Prophet] continued to acknowledge the Prophet before his appearance; but when he appeared, they differed: some of them affirmed, and some of them denied.

And His saying: ﴿a messenger from Allah﴾, meaning: he is a messenger from Allah. It was also said: (the meaning is) "until there came to them a messenger from Allah."

And His saying: ﴿reciting purified pages﴾, meaning: what is in the pages (ṣuḥuf). And His saying: ﴿purified﴾, meaning: free from alteration (taghyīr), substitution (tabdīl), defilement (idnās), and impurity (injās).

In His saying: ﴿Therein are upright books﴾, meaning: rulings that are correct and just. The word "kitab" (book) can carry the meaning of "hukm" (judgment, ruling), and "kutub" (books) can carry the meaning of "ahkam" (rulings). In the story of the hired man (al-'asif), the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will judge between you two by the Book of Allah," meaning: by the judgment of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾ — i.e., concerning the matter of the Prophet and what he brought.

And His saying: ﴿except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾ — i.e., the clear proofs, the demonstrations, and the indications.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 98, verse 5:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Yet they were commanded only to worship Allah, making the religion sincerely His, inclining to truth﴾. The meaning of ḥanīf has already been mentioned. It has also been said: if the one addressed is a Muslim, then it means ḥājj (one who performs the pilgrimage); and if the one addressed is a non-Muslim, then it means Islam. The meaning is: they were commanded to be ḥunafā' (inclining to truth). If the address is to the Muslims, then what is meant is that they should be ḥujjāj (pilgrims); and if the address is to the disbelievers, then what is meant is that they should be Muslims.

And His words: ﴿and establish the prayer and give the zakah, and that is the upright religion﴾. That is, that is the upright community (al-millah al-qayyimah). It has also been said: the religion of the upright nation that is firm upon the truth. And it has been said: the religion of the upright community.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 98, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. They are the worst of creatures.﴾ It is read with the hamza and without the hamza. The reading with the hamza is from "bara'a Allah al-khalq" (God originated the creation), and the reading without the hamza is from al-bara (al-buraa), which is dust (al-turab), meaning: the worst of those created from dust. The Arabs say: "bifika al-buraa wa al-tharaa" (may your mouth be filled with dust and earth).

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds—they are the best of creation﴾ — we have already mentioned it. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from al-Mukhtar ibn Falfal, from Anas ibn Malik: "A man said to the Prophet, 'O best of creation!' He said: 'That is Ibrahim—may Allah's blessings be upon him.'" Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi reported it in his Jami', and said: "It is sahih gharib."

Wa qawluhu: "Jazāʾuhum ʿinda rabbihim jannātu ʿadnin tajrī..." (Surah al-Bayyinah 98:8 begins here with the verse's first part, which the commentary quotes.)

Let me translate the passage as it stands.

And His saying: ﴿Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence (ʿAdn), beneath which rivers flow﴾. Ibn ʿUmar said: Allah created four things with His own Hand: the Pen, the Throne, the Garden of ʿAdn, and Adam, upon him be blessings and peace. And He said to the rest of things: "Be," and they were.

And His saying: ﴿Wherein they abide forever, beneath which rivers flow, forever therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾: that is, He is pleased with their deeds, and they are pleased with His reward.

And His saying: ﴿That is for whoever fears his Lord﴾: that is, whoever fears his Lord.
